body: [{"streamId":"01a0ddfb-a8f8-72af-a1db-6d9de4928176","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskAdded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0ddfb-a8f8-72af-a1db-6d9de4928176\u0022,\u0022ProjectId\u0022:\u002201a0a27f-abdf-7731-84aa-d604e9bc53ca\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:\u0022The carvana walk stops paging at a result page that says \\u0027No exact matches\\u0027 and never takes a link from its similar-vehicles padding, and the search\\u0027s stated car count bounds how many links the pages contribute in total, so a pair\\u0027s cap is spent on cars the facets asked for\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022WalkSite gains a nullable pattern (name it for what it is, for example ExhaustedSearchPattern) that WalkSearchPages.CollectLinksAsync checks on every page including the first: a page whose text matches it contributes no links and ends paging, with a console line saying the search ran out of exact matches on page N; carvana sets it to match \\u0027No exact matches\\u0027; cars.com and autotrader set none and behave exactly as before; proven by a WalkSearchPages test over a three-page sequence cut from the recorded pages (16 cars, then a No-exact-matches page, then a repeat) that yields only page-one links and requests no third page\u0022,\u0022carvana sets WalkSite.MatchCountPattern to read its stated count (\\u002716 cars\\u0027), and CollectLinksAsync applies a stated count from the first page as the search\\u0027s total bound across every page it follows, taking links in page order and stopping when the bound is reached, so a first page stating 16 cars but showing 18 results contributes at most 16; the existing autotrader per-page behavior is unchanged; proven by tests for both the one-page and the paged case\u0022,\u0022The recorded carvana Insight pages from walks/carvana/20260926-121057/insight (search.txt and search-2.txt) are cut down into fixtures under tests/Odonomics.Tests/fixtures; the README\\u0027s Carvana paging text says paging ends at a No-exact-matches page and the stated count bounds the links; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Reported by run session odonomics-59 on 2026-09-26 during walk run 5 on main 17ebf27 (notes/run-session-2026-09-22.md, Gaps found), verified by the orchestrator against the recorded pages under ~/Library/Application Support/Odonomics/walks/carvana/20260926-121057/insight/: search.txt states \\u002716 cars\\u0027 and \\u0027Showing 18 results\\u0027; search-2.txt carries \\u0027No exact matches\\u0027 and \\u0027Check out similar vehicles\\u0027 followed by seven page-one Insights repeated, two Insights over the mileage facet, a 2023 Civic and two 2025 Civic Hybrids; search-3.txt is byte-identical to search-2.txt, which is what stopped the paging (added == 0). Result: carvana / Honda Insight, 21 pages, 18 saved, 3 dropped (wrong model), so three detail visits went to Civics. Code: src/Odonomics/Walk/WalkSearchPages.cs CollectLinksAsync(site, searchUrl, poolSize, loadPageAsync, onLaterPageFailed, ct) loops pages while pageUrlFor is set, the pool is below poolSize, and the page added a link; src/Odonomics/Walk/WalkSites.cs defines WalkSite with PagedSearchUrl (carvana only) and MatchCountPattern (autotrader only, added in commit 25021d5 with tests in tests/Odonomics.Tests/Walk/AutotraderWalkTests.cs; read its MatchCountIn and the link-taking method for the precedent). Carvana detail links match /vehicle/\\u003Cdigits\\u003E. Keep the existing repeat-page stop as a backstop.
